text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Tuesday.

LONDON - Leading British shares ended higher, with the FTSE 100 closing at a new record -- fuelled by strong futures and gilt market. the perception that cash-rich institutional funds are poised to funnel money back into UK equity market in the last quarter of the year renewed hopes that the FTSE 100 will decisively charge through the 4,000 level this week. The benchmark FTSE 100 index added 38.5 points to finish at a new closing high at 3,992.2.

FRANKFURT - German shares ended calm bourse dealing stable, seen remaining rangebound in later trade, investor activity remains lacklustre after last week's record run and upside seen limited. The 30-share DAX index ended up 3.88 points to 2,655.73. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 2,654.34.

PARIS - French shares finished with losses with the market consolidating after recent strong gains, the market largely shrugged off a weaker-than-expected report from the U.S. National Association of Purchasing Managers, stocks in the luxury goods sector rose, while oils and Air Liquide declined. The blue-chip CAC-40 index ended down 9.60 points or 0.45 percent to 2,123.21.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended an uneventful session marginally higher, buoyed by major pharmaceuticals, volumes were moderate with investors probably already concentrating on Friday's U.S. jobs data. The All-share Swiss Performance Index gained 0.8 points to end at 2,394.75.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks buckled under profit-taking pressure, putting an end to the five-day winning streak, brokers said profit-taking battered the Nikkei average for most of the day, but sentiment was still firm and the falls well cushioned. The benchmark Nikkei 225 fell 93.43 points or 0.43 percent to 21,462.97.
HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks closed higher, with the market showing resilience as some investors tried to take profits. The Hang Seng index rose 18.79 points to 11,921.22.

SYDNEY - The Australian stock market closed lower as sliding metal prices pushed the resources sector lower, just offsetting industrial stocks which gained ground on continued support for the banking sector. The All Ordinaries index fell 4.9 points to 2,285.5.

JOHANNESBURG - After a day of baffling trade which saw South African shares suffer earlier, shares astonished dealers by recovering in the afternoon to end firm. "It was a strange and confusing day," a dealer said, shares started weak and extended losses, dragged down by falling bullion and a feeble rand. The All-share index added 18.2 points to 6,896.2, Industrials put on 3.5 points to 8,134.1 and Golds were up 23.5 points to 1,677.2.
